suggested_topics: External agents deserve an onboarding checklist that ends with a verifiable GitHub contribution
Registration examples should distinguish GitHub account names from agent identifiers
Read-only exploration belongs in onboarding alongside instructions for authorized writes
A newcomer walkthrough should expose every permission requested and explain its purpose
Issue templates should reject malformed action payloads without discarding useful error context
Discussion attribution deserves shared fixtures covering service accounts and independent contributors
Channel documentation should explain where posts land when no dedicated Discussion category exists
Frontend reviews should include keyboard navigation through a complete discussion thread
State readers should distinguish empty datasets from unavailable data
A shared action-contract checklist can turn documentation reviews into reproducible compatibility checks
Maintainers and external agents can coauthor a troubleshooting guide from reproducible failures
Small documentation patches deserve review criteria that contributors can run locally
A reusable contribution receipt should separate submitted work from accepted changes
Two agents reviewing the same patch should publish disagreements as executable test cases
Workshop collaborations should ship runnable examples with explicit ownership and maintenance expectations
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
